_about: Species descriptions shipped in the export bundle and returned with each prediction so GeoFlora can show what the plant is. Keyed by species_id. Drafted with AI assistance from general botanical knowledge; not yet checked against a cited flora or by a botanist. Set review_status to 'reviewed' and fill reviewed_by/reviewed_date only after someone has checked a description against the references.

GF-SP-0001.summary: A fast-growing perennial shrub that forms dense thickets on roadsides, fallow land, pastures and forest edges. It scrambles over other plants and spreads by wind-blown seed.
identifying_features: Shrub usually 1.5-3 m tall; stems can scramble higher over surrounding vegetation.
Leaves opposite, triangular to ovate, coarsely toothed, with three prominent veins from the leaf base; strong smell when crushed.
Flower heads cylindrical, about 1 cm long, in clusters at the branch tips; florets white to pale lilac, with no petal-like rays.
Seeds carry a tuft of bristles and form grey-brown fluffy heads when mature.
GF-SP-0001.why_it_matters: Smothers crops, pasture and native vegetation, and dry thickets increase fire risk. Listed among the '100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species' (Lowe et al. 2000).

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: A small soft herb, usually under 1 m, with rounder, fluffier blue to white flower heads and no strong three-vein leaf pattern.
A twining vine with heart-shaped leaves on long stalks and many tiny white flower heads.

references: Lowe S., Browne M., Boudjelas S., De Poorter M. (2000). 100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species. IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group.

GF-SP-0002.summary: An aromatic, often prickly shrub with small clustered flowers in mixed colours. It is widely planted as an ornamental and escapes into pastures, roadsides and forest edges, where it forms dense thickets.
identifying_features: Shrub usually 1-2 m tall (sometimes taller); stems square in cross-section, often with small hooked prickles.
Leaves opposite, ovate, rough to the touch, with toothed edges; strong smell when crushed.
Small tubular flowers in flat-topped clusters, often of mixed colours (yellow, orange, pink, red) that change as they age.
Clusters of small round berries, green turning glossy purple-black when ripe.
GF-SP-0002.why_it_matters: Forms dense thickets that crowd out native plants. Leaves and unripe fruit are toxic to livestock. Listed among the '100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species' (Lowe et al. 2000).

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: A low trailing or creeping plant with smaller leaves and flowers that are uniformly lilac-purple (or white), not mixed colours.
Blue-violet flowers in drooping sprays and hanging clusters of orange-yellow berries; leaves smooth, not rough.

references: Lowe S., Browne M., Boudjelas S., De Poorter M. (2000). 100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species. IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group.

common_names: Water lily (local name, not a true water lily)
GF-SP-0003.summary: A free-floating aquatic plant that multiplies quickly and forms large mats on rivers, lakes, canals and ponds.
identifying_features: Floats on the water surface as rosettes of glossy, rounded leaves.
Leaf stalks often swollen and spongy, acting as floats.
Dark, feathery roots hang in the water beneath the plant.
Spikes of lavender flowers; the upper petal has a violet-blue patch with a yellow spot in the centre.
GF-SP-0003.why_it_matters: Dense mats block waterways and boats, hinder fishing, clog irrigation and drainage, reduce light and oxygen in the water, and can worsen flooding. Listed among the '100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species' as Eichhornia crassipes (Lowe et al. 2000).

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Rooted in mud (for example in rice fields), not floating; leaf stalks not swollen; smaller blue-violet flowers without a yellow spot.
Water lettuce: rosettes of pale green, velvety, ridged leaves with no stalks, and tiny hidden flowers.

references: Lowe S., Browne M., Boudjelas S., De Poorter M. (2000). 100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species. IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group.

GF-SP-0101.summary: A small, soft, hairy annual herb common in fields, gardens and roadsides, with fluffy blue to white flower heads.
identifying_features: Herb usually 30-80 cm tall with soft, hairy stems.
Leaves opposite, ovate, toothed and hairy, on short stalks.
Small round, fluffy flower heads (about 5 mm) in dense clusters, blue-lilac to white.
GF-SP-0101.why_it_matters: Not a GeoFlora target species. Its ecological status in the Philippines is unresolved in this project's catalog, so it is not labelled invasive or non-invasive here. It is the plant most often confused with Hagonoy (Chromolaena odorata).

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Hagonoy is a tall shrub with cylindrical flower heads and leaves with three strong veins from the base.

GF-SP-0102.summary: A fast-growing twining vine that climbs over shrubs, trees and crops and can smother them.
identifying_features: Thin twining stems that climb over other plants.
Leaves opposite, heart-shaped, on long stalks.
Many tiny white flower heads in loose clusters.
GF-SP-0102.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (Box 2.1, as mile-a-minute weed or uoko). It smothers crops and other plants and releases chemicals that suppress them.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Hagonoy is an upright shrub, not a vine, and its leaves are triangular with three strong veins, not heart-shaped.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0103.summary: A low, trailing relative of Lantana camara, often grown as an ornamental ground cover or hanging plant.
identifying_features: Low, spreading or trailing stems.
Small ovate, toothed, rough leaves.
Small flat clusters of lilac-purple (sometimes white) flowers, all one colour.
GF-SP-0103.why_it_matters: Not a GeoFlora target species. Its ecological status in the Philippines is unresolved in this project's catalog, so it is not labelled invasive or non-invasive here.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Lantana camara is an upright shrub with larger leaves and mixed-colour flower clusters (yellow, orange, pink, red).

GF-SP-0104.summary: A shrub or small tree widely planted as an ornamental and as hedges, including golden-leaved forms.
identifying_features: Shrub or small tree; leaves opposite, smooth and glossy (golden in some garden forms).
Light blue to violet (sometimes white) flowers in drooping sprays.
Hanging clusters of round orange-yellow berries.
GF-SP-0104.why_it_matters: Not a GeoFlora target species. Its ecological status in the Philippines is unresolved in this project's catalog, so it is not labelled invasive or non-invasive here. Its berries are reported to be toxic if eaten.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Lantana has rough leaves, flat-topped mixed-colour flower clusters and purple-black berries.

GF-SP-0105.summary: A free-floating aquatic plant forming rosettes like small heads of lettuce; can form dense mats on still water.
identifying_features: Rosettes of thick, pale green, velvety leaves with strong parallel ridges.
No leaf stalks; leaves widen towards the tip.
Feathery roots hang underneath; flowers tiny and hidden in the centre.
GF-SP-0105.why_it_matters: Not a GeoFlora target species. Its ecological status in the Philippines is unresolved in this project's catalog, so it is not labelled invasive or non-invasive here.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Water hyacinth has glossy round leaves on swollen stalks and showy lavender flower spikes.

GF-SP-0106.summary: An aquatic herb rooted in mud, common in rice fields, ditches and wet ground.
identifying_features: Rooted in mud, not floating.
Glossy, lance- to heart-shaped leaves on long stalks with a sheathing base; stalks not swollen.
Short clusters of blue-violet flowers without a yellow spot.
GF-SP-0106.why_it_matters: Not a GeoFlora target species. Its ecological status in the Philippines is unresolved in this project's catalog, so it is not labelled invasive or non-invasive here.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Water hyacinth floats freely, has swollen spongy leaf stalks, and its upper petal has a yellow spot.

GF-SP-0107.summary: An aquatic herb rooted in shallow water and mud of rice fields, ditches and swamps; eaten as a vegetable in parts of Southeast Asia.
identifying_features: Erect, broad oval, bright green leaves on long triangular stalks.
Flowers with three pale yellow petals edged in white, in clusters on long stalks.
Grows rooted in mud, not floating.
GF-SP-0107.why_it_matters: Not a GeoFlora target species. Its ecological status in the Philippines is unresolved in this project's catalog, so it is not labelled invasive or non-invasive here.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Water hyacinth floats, has swollen leaf stalks and lavender flowers.

GF-SP-0206.native_range: Widespread in the Old World tropics and subtropics
GF-SP-0206.summary: A tough perennial grass that spreads by underground rhizomes and wind-blown seed, forming dense grasslands.
identifying_features: Upright grass usually 0.3-1.2 m tall, growing in dense stands.
Narrow, stiff leaves with a pale midrib that is often off-centre; edges feel rough.
Silky, white, fluffy flower plumes, typically 5-20 cm long.
GF-SP-0206.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (p. 9). NISSAP notes it now covers about 20% of the country and burns easily in the dry season, but also that some botanists consider it naturalized.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Look for the silky white plume; without it, cogon is hard to tell from other grasses.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0303.summary: A fast-growing small tree planted for fodder, firewood and reforestation that forms dense pure stands.
identifying_features: Shrub or small tree, usually 3-10 m tall.
Feathery, twice-divided (bipinnate) leaves with many small leaflets.
Round, creamy-white pom-pom flower heads.
Clusters of flat, strap-shaped pods that turn brown.
GF-SP-0303.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (Box 2.1 and Table 3.2). It forms pure stands that are hard to remove and prevent native forest regrowth.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Ipil-ipil has round white pom-pom flowers and flat brown pods in clusters.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0304.summary: A large ornamental and shade tree with big orange-red flowers that invades disturbed land and forest.
identifying_features: Tree that can grow over 20 m tall.
Large leaves divided into several pairs of leaflets.
Big, cup-shaped, orange-red flowers in clusters at the branch tips.
Long, boat-shaped pods that release papery winged seeds.
GF-SP-0304.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (Box 2.1 and Fig. 2.5). It forms thickets that out-compete surrounding plants.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Fire tree has fern-like feathery leaves and flat, five-petalled flowers, not large cup-shaped ones.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0305.summary: A fast-spreading shrub or small tree that forms thickets in disturbed areas.
identifying_features: Shrub or small tree, usually 3-7 m tall, with jointed stems.
Lance-shaped, rough leaves with an uneven base, arranged alternately.
Curved, finger-like, cream-coloured flower spikes.
GF-SP-0305.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (Box 2.1 and Fig. 2.4). It forms thickets, disrupts forest regrowth and reduces biodiversity.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Ikmo is a climbing vine with smooth, heart-shaped leaves; buyo-buyo is an upright shrub with rough, narrow leaves.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0308.summary: A floating water fern that multiplies quickly and covers still water with thick mats.
identifying_features: Floating fern with pairs of oval leaves, 1-4 cm long, that fold upward as mats thicken.
Upper leaf surface covered with tiny water-repelling hairs.
Brown, root-like submerged leaves hang below.
GF-SP-0308.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (p. 9 and Box 2.1). Its mats reduce water flow, light and oxygen, and harm fish and other aquatic life.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Water lettuce forms rosettes of larger, ridged, velvety leaves, not small paired oval leaves.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0311.summary: A fast-growing tree once planted for fibre that escaped and invades young secondary forests.
identifying_features: Tree up to about 10-15 m tall.
Leaves vary on the same tree: heart-shaped or deeply lobed, rough above and soft-hairy below.
Round female flower heads that ripen into orange-red fruit balls.
GF-SP-0311.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (Box 2.1 and Table 3.2). It invades young secondary forests and slows natural forest regrowth.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Mulberry has smoother leaves and elongated, berry-like fruits, not round orange-red balls.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0312.native_range: North-eastern Australia, New Guinea and eastern Indonesia
GF-SP-0312.summary: A fast-growing tree widely planted for forestry and restoration that produces many seeds.
identifying_features: Large tree with straight trunk.
Broad, leaf-like phyllodes with about four strong lengthwise veins.
Cream-white flower spikes.
Tightly coiled pods.
GF-SP-0312.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (Box 2.1 and Table 3.2). It is considered a threat to indigenous plants.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Auri has narrower, curved phyllodes and golden-yellow flower spikes.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0313.summary: A large timber tree widely planted for reforestation in the Philippines.
identifying_features: Tall tree with a buttressed trunk.
Leaves divided into several pairs of glossy, pointed leaflets.
Large, upright, egg-shaped woody fruits that split into five parts.
Brown seeds with a long papery wing.
GF-SP-0313.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (p. 9 and Table 3.2, as a reforestation species). NISSAP notes that the dominance of such exotic reforestation trees has changed parts of the Philippine landscape.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Small-leaf mahogany has smaller leaflets and smaller fruits.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0314.summary: A fast-growing deciduous timber tree widely planted for reforestation.
identifying_features: Tree with smooth, pale grey bark.
Large, broad, heart-shaped leaves in opposite pairs.
Brownish-yellow, trumpet-shaped flowers.
Plum-like fruits that turn yellow when ripe.
GF-SP-0314.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (p. 9 and Table 3.2, as a reforestation species). NISSAP notes that the dominance of such exotic reforestation trees has changed parts of the Philippine landscape.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Teak has very large rough leaves and small white flowers in big branched clusters.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0315.native_range: Mindanao, Sulawesi, New Guinea and nearby islands
GF-SP-0315.summary: A tall, fast-growing tree known for its smooth, multicoloured peeling bark.
identifying_features: Tall tree with a straight trunk.
Smooth bark that peels in strips, showing streaks of green, blue, purple, orange and brown.
Lance-shaped leaves and small white flowers.
GF-SP-0315.why_it_matters: NISSAP lists Eucalyptus among the exotic reforestation species (p. 9, Table 3.2), but E. deglupta is widely reported as native to Mindanao. Its invasive status in the Philippines should be checked before it is treated as invasive.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Most other eucalyptus species lack the bright rainbow-coloured bark.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf

GF-SP-0316.native_range: Northern Australia, New Guinea and eastern Indonesia
GF-SP-0316.summary: A fast-growing tree widely planted for reforestation and shade.
identifying_features: Tree with dense, drooping foliage.
Narrow, curved, sickle-shaped phyllodes with several lengthwise veins.
Golden-yellow flower spikes.
Twisted, coiled pods showing black seeds with orange stalks.
GF-SP-0316.why_it_matters: Listed by DENR-BMB's National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020-2030 among invasive alien plants in the Philippines (p. 9, as a reforestation species). Not yet a verified target in this project's catalog. NISSAP notes that the dominance of such exotic reforestation trees has changed parts of the Philippine landscape.

lookalikes.how_to_tell_apart: Mangium has broader phyllodes and cream-white flower spikes.

references: DENR-BMB (2020). National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan 2020-2030. https://www.philchm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/NISSAP-2020-2030.pdf
